step_by_step_reasoning: The whiteboard architecture shows a multi-tier data ingestion and storage pipeline between a Customer AWS environment and Splunk's AWS environment. On the Customer side, data originates from a data source (UserCompanyDataStream), Lambda, Kinesis Firehose, and an S3 bucket. Data flows into Splunk's environment via two Elastic Load Balancers (ELB): standard HEC data and Lambda logs pass through the top ELB, while Kinesis Data Firehose routes through the bottom ELB. Both ELBs forward traffic to Splunk's EC2 caching/indexing tier in an Auto Scaling group. EC2 offloads infrequently searched data to an S3 bucket and archives cold data to Glacier (S3). Splunk S3 also supports dynamic data self-storage exporting back into the Customer S3 bucket.
